text:
Alex Chen: RFC follow-up: prototype idea to attach a small patch-sidecar to safetensors bundles (extension .patchidx) that lists chunk ranges + patch ops so loaders can stream only the changed bytes when switching between model builds or quant variants.
Mira Patel: sounds promising. How would older loaders behave when they encounter the sidecar?
Alex Chen: sidecars are optional. legacy loaders ignore unknown files. new loader reads manifest that references the main .safetensors and any sidecars. If compatibility mismatch, loader falls back to full fetch.
Samir Gupta: what patch primitives are we supporting? binary xor diffs? full replacement?
Alex Chen: start small: support either "replace" for chunk-level full replacement and an "xor" delta op for small bitwise changes. Keep ops simple to avoid model-format decoding.
Jia Li: chunk sizing tradeoff? small chunks = better patch coverage but more range-requests. Any numbers in mind?
Alex Chen: initial defaults: 128KB chunks. We can tune per-model family; include chunk_size in sidecar header so runtime can plan requests.
Lucas Moreno: warmup hints are important. If we only patch sparsely, cold-start still needs priority for token-critical prefixes. Add a separate .warmhint file with hot-prefix offsets and checksum of the patched shard.
Mira Patel: delta application cost: applying patches will consume CPU and temporary disk. For quantized blobs, patching could be tricky if quant encoding isn't deterministic. Do we want to limit patches to post-quantized bytes?
Samir Gupta: yes, restrict to byte-level ops on the on-disk representation. That means model build must be deterministic for quant outputs. Build pipeline should optionally emit sidecar by diffing against a canonical base.
Jia Li: eviction and coherence: if we evict a chunk that's a dependency for a patched region, the coordinator should mark the region dirty so prefetch can restore dependencies in order. Hints should include dependency lists.
Alex Chen: agreed. We'll include a lightweight dependency map in .warmhint: for each hot-prefix, list chunk ids required, and a version tag.
Olivia Park: naming nit: maybe call the ops file "patch-index" and the hints file "warm-hints" to be explicit in the console and docs.
Alex Chen: fine with that. Loader API sketch (manifest-driven):
[manifest text embedded]
{
  "primary": "s3://models/rl-release/v3/opt-7b.safetensors",
  "sidecars": ["s3://models/rl-release/v3/opt-7b.patchidx", "s3://models/rl-release/v3/opt-7b.warmhint"],
  "policy": "delta-stream-prefer",
  "chunk_hint": 131072
}
Samir Gupta: error handling: if patch-apply fails, record metric patch.apply.error and fetch the original shard. Also need a retry backoff for transient S3 range failures.
Lucas Moreno: rollout plan: feature-flag at runtime, start with small models (<=1.5B) and gating on build.delta.ratio >= 0.25. Instrument metrics: patch.bytes_saved, patch.apply.ms, cold.first_token_latency.
Mira Patel: how to ensure atomicity? we can follow existing weight-swap pattern: materialize patched shard to ephemeral path, fsync, rename into place, and only then update active pointer. Add an apply-lock/lease so concurrent loaders don't race.
Jia Li: tests: unit fuzz on patches, integration with 206 range partials and intermittent failures, canary that forces a corrupt patch to ensure fallback works.
Olivia Park: storage overhead question: we should compute patch storage vs network savings. If patch size is >30% of shard, skip sidecar. Make this a build-time gate.
Samir Gupta: also think about security: sidecars must be signed similarly to model artifacts. Verify signature before applying.
Alex Chen: good call. Add sidecar signing to artifact pipeline and verify signature in loader. Failure -> treat as incompatible and fall back.
deploy-bot: CI: patch-index schema test added, unit checks green, integration queued in canary :rocket:
Lucas Moreno: ops note: collect delta-apply cpu spike telemetry and set alert thresholds during canary. Keep slow-path budget small (<=5% traffic).
Mira Patel: I'm 👍 if we: 1) restrict to simple byte ops, 2) require build determinism, 3) atomic apply + lease, 4) gating by measured savings. I'll draft short RFC fragment for on-disk format and loader boundary.
Alex Chen: I'll start a spike to emit patchidx from the build tool and a minimal loader that streams range requests and applies xor/replacements. Thanks all.
Olivia Park: include experiment template in RFC — we want numbers before promoting to Dedicated/Private. :eyes:
